summary: The root ورق (waraqa) primarily refers to leaves. A "waraq" is a leaf, and "waraqa" can describe a tree with abundant leaves, or one that is leafy and provides ample shade.
lane: شَجَرٌ وَارِقٌ ذ Trees having leaves: (Msb:) [or leafy trees; trees having many leaves; for] شَجَرَةٌ وَارِقَةٌ (TA) and and (S, K, TA) signify a tree having many leaves. (S, K, TA.) And شَجَرَةٌ وَارِقَةُ الظِّلَالِ [ A tree having leafy coverings or shades ]. (K in art. غيل .)

headwords.def: وَرِقٌ Silver, whether coined or not: (AO, TA:) or coined dirhems; (S, K;) coined silver. (Mgh.) See عَيْنٌ.
أَوْرَاق, pl. of وَرَقٌ, meaning أَحْدَاث: see قَعْبٌ.

شَجَرٌ وَارِقٌ Trees having leaves: (Msb:) [or leafy trees; trees having many leaves; for] شَجَرَةٌ وَارِقَةٌ (TA) and and (S, K, TA) signify a tree having many leaves. (S, K, TA.) And شَجَرَةٌ وَارِقَةُ الظِّلَالِ [ A tree having leafy coverings or shades ]. (K in art. غيل.)

أَوْرَقُ, applied to a camel, White inclining to black; i. e. of a dusky white hue: or rather, simply, duskish; or dusky; (S, K;) or of a colour like that of ashes. (T, Mgh, Msb.) See أَحْمَرُ and خُطَبَانِىٌّ. أَوْرَقُ Ashes. (K.) See an ex. a verse cited voce عُنَّةٌ, last sentence.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
